gates.title: Requirement/evidence graph
observations: coverage names unpinned requirements (0.9.0)

2026-11-02 independent adversarial review of `repo-ai coverage` against C11 (calls into assess/for_mission with constructed records): green needs exact fail->pass or pass->pass on a fresh, comparable PASS (identical test ids, pinned test inputs and skip sets), outcome vocabulary allow-listed; found 3 high (VERIFIED rows and an empty follow-up list under a STALE or INCONCLUSIVE headline; no link from requirements to changed code although the mission measures which changed lines the tests ran; scoped pre-existing failures dropped), 3 medium (silent suffix binding to another file's test; one test for several requirements unflagged; the declaration is not frozen) and 4 low. Fixed in the coverage PR: rows downgraded to UNVERIFIED_*, changed code no test ran and pre-existing failures listed as other_obligations (headline at most ACCEPTANCE_PARTIAL), suffix and shared-test flags, failure-before-skip ordering

2026-11-02 `do --requirements FILE` freezes the declaration with the mission record before it runs; `coverage ID` assesses it and reports declaration FROZEN_WITH_MISSION (written before this mission ran), FROZEN_AFTER_PRIOR_RUN (an earlier mission on the same source and proposal had recorded outcomes) or SUPPLIED_AT_ASSESSMENT; refused without --run, with --resume/--from-handoff/--tournament and for an already-recorded mission; reviewed independently (a re-run loophole, silent drops, malformed entries found and fixed); end-to-end CLI tests on a real replay mission

2026-11-03 per requirement (pytest, frozen declaration only): the exercise run's tracer records which changed executable lines ran while each pytest test ran (sys.monitoring line events re-armed at each test; watched = changed files) and those run outside any test; coverage lists each requirement's changed_lines_run, the changed lines only undeclared tests ran and those run at import/collection. An independent review of the first version found its obligation (a verified change requirement whose tests ran no changed line) false in common fixes: import-time lines (constants, default arguments, decorator arguments), shared fixtures credited to the first test, subprocess tests, xdist; it was removed, and the mapping is informational only (no row, obligation or headline effect); a spawned process or an early stop marks the record incomplete; re-review: the per-test record comes from a second run in the time left (so a slow per-test run can no longer turn the measurement UNMEASURED and add an obligation), and multiprocessing, os.fork and early stops (-x/--maxfail: fewer tests ran than were collected) mark it incomplete

2026-11-03 queue row 32: each run of a shared fixture's setup is credited to the tests whose call ran with it active (per-run tokens; override chains, dependencies and getfixturevalue; line events re-armed at fixture boundaries so 3.12+ and older interpreters agree; directly run lines fill the cap first). A review of the first version found it merged parametrized/per-class runs, credited skipped tests and could push direct lines out of the cap; all fixed with regression tests (params, class scope, skip, override, getfixturevalue, two fixtures, cap); a second review round found an override that ignores its parent credited with the parent's cached run (fixed: only definitions actually used, the active one and those it extends) and runs no test claimed appearing nowhere (now outside any test)
limits: per-requirement changed-line mapping: pytest only, only for missions run with a frozen declaration, not Node or container runs; attribution is by time window (each run of a shared fixture's setup is credited to the tests whose call ran with it active, its teardown to the test it runs after, a thread's work to whichever test is running, child processes are not seen, import-time lines belong to no test unless the module is first imported inside a test), so it is informational; under Python <3.12 (settrace) a function's def line counts as run when it is called, unlike 3.12+

a frozen declaration shows only that it preceded this mission's run: outcomes known from tests run outside repo-ai are invisible to it, and its digest is unkeyed (accidental edits only, not a rewritten local store); a declaration supplied at assessment time is labelled SUPPLIED_AT_ASSESSMENT; prior-run detection sees only missions still in the store on the same source with the same proposal or candidate diff
test-id resolution: a bare name matched by suffix is flagged, not refused; node and parametrized ids with '::' can match partially; a leaf name never matches a `describe > leaf` id
one test mapped to several requirements is flagged (shared_tests), not refused: all of them can still reach ACCEPTANCE_MAPPED_ALL
gates.next_action: Node per test file; a rule on the mapping only after an independent review of fixture-scope attribution on real projects

gates.title: Performance
gates.environment: GitHub ubuntu-latest (4 vCPU), bwrap; earlier: macOS
observations: verify 1.44–2.31x slower than native in 3/5 held-out cases (historical)

2026-10-31 speed-v1 (preregistered; 5 pinned pure-Python projects x 6 real upstream commits; GitHub ubuntu runner, bwrap): verify --run cold 1.84x the native suite (geometric mean), slower on 24 of 30; the 6 'faster' were verify runs that failed (more-itertools full-suite-failed). Overhead median +0.63 s; reuse 0.20 s. No false assurance, with little power (only 5 of 30 native suites failed, 2 of them contaminated by a harness defect); verify failed natively passing tests in 14 (pyjwt network-denied, more-itertools and humanize unexplained, marshmallow name-matched files)

2026-11-01 profile of the fixed overhead (macOS, Apple Silicon; a 40-test pytest project; not a re-run of speed-v1): a comment-only verify --run spent ~0.68 s of 0.92 s in 18 sequential git subprocesses (35 ms each through Apple's /usr/bin/git launcher stub, 17 ms direct) and ~80 ms importing the mission runtime and provider adapters to build the argument parser. Fixed: the stub is resolved once per process (gitbin.git(): DEVELOPER_DIR, the xcode-select link, else xcode-select -p) and those imports are lazy. verify --run 965 -> 636 ms (comment-only), 1,370 -> 992 ms (behaviour change, full suite), reuse 544 -> 330 ms; Claude hooks ~150 -> 67-81 ms (session-start 324 -> 205 ms). Remaining duplicate git reads are the before/after source-tree checks and are kept. Linux overhead (speed-v1) is not re-measured by this

2026-11-01 speed-v1 run 3 (Amendment 3, a replication stated before the run; GitHub run 41306386452, commit 8cd3afd, different runner CPU): cold 2.23x the native suite (geometric mean), slower on 30 of 30 (run 2: 1.84x, 24 of 30); without more-itertools (measured differently: targeted in run 3, full in run 2) 2.61x vs 2.64x; absolute overhead confounded by the CPU change, not compared. Exit codes agree with the native suite on 23 of 30 (run 2: 16): more-itertools 6/6 and humanize f772e59b now agree, consistent with the 0.11.4/0.11.5 fixes but not isolated by the runs (more-itertools full suite seen passing once); pyjwt 6 (pre-existing, consistent with the denied network) and marshmallow 2fc8207d still disagree, and 2fc8207d still gives two verdicts for one state (cold exit 1, --rerun exit 0); no false assurance, little power (0 of 4 failing native suites, all configuration or collection crashes)

2026-11-01 #65: when verify matches pytest tests by name, the plan names test files under the project's norecursedirs (read from the file pytest would use), so a targeted/full disagreement like marshmallow 2fc8207d is explained in the product; a note only, nothing removed

2026-11-01 Linux profile (scripts/profile_verify.py on GitHub runners, 40-test generated project with its own .venv; profile runs 41340493434 before, 41340833864 after): git was negligible on Linux (18 calls, 0.03 s); the two source-tree snapshots took ~0.62 of 0.70 s (profiled) of a comment-only verify, mostly pathlib relative_to over ~2,000 venv entries (cProfile inflates such code; unprofiled comment-only 0.34 -> 0.23 s on a slower runner). Fixed by carrying relative prefixes (oracle-tested): ratio to the native suite on ubuntu 2.16x -> 1.12x (comment-only), 3.54x -> 2.38x (behaviour change; the sandboxed pytest, ~0.2 of 0.49 s, is now the largest single part; most of that ratio drop is the slower runner's larger native time, absolute 0.55 -> 0.49 s); macOS 2.86x -> 1.71x, 4.17x -> 3.04x. One run per platform, runners differed (native suite +25-32% in the after run), so ratios are reported, not absolute times; speed-v1 not re-run

2026-11-01 speed-v1 run 4 (Amendment 4, a replication stated before the run, on 0.11.7 after the snapshot fix; GitHub run 41360280119, same CPU model as run 2): cold 2.00x the native suite, slower on 30 of 30 (still not faster by the reading rule); without more-itertools 2.26x (run 2 2.64x, run 3 2.61x; strategies differ within that subset too). Decided after the run (the amendment compares ratios only): with native times close to run 2's on the same CPU model, median overhead +0.38 s vs run 2's +0.63 s (per project pyjwt 0.42->0.18 s, itsdangerous 0.58->0.30 s, humanize 1.10->0.83 s, marshmallow 1.79->1.43 s); confounded by other repo-ai changes, the harness (pre- vs post-Amendment 2) and the host (run 4's native suites up to 12% faster, pyjwt unchanged). Agreement 24 of 30: the one change from run 3 is marshmallow 2fc8207d choosing the full strategy this time (a strategy effect, not a fix); only pyjwt's network-dependent changes disagree; no false assurance, little power (0 of 4 failing native suites, all configuration or collection crashes)

2026-11-01 speed-v1 run 5 (Amendment 5: strategy reasons, full-suite command, verify's commands and sandbox_network_suspected recorded): 1.96x geometric mean cold ratio, slower than native on 28 of 30 (reading rule: not faster), overhead median +0.32 s, exit agreement 24 of 30 (the 6 pyjwt disagreements all sandbox_network_suspected). Recorded reasons show the strategy turns on close estimates measured in the same run (tenths of a second, some within the tie margin) and on missing per-file measurements (9 cold calls, 4 of them a project's first change); within run 5 the cold and --rerun calls on one state chose different strategies on 4 of 30 changes (recorded); that earlier cross-run flips happened this way is inferred. marshmallow 2fc8207d: cold and --rerun ran full with the same command (the reuse call reported the cold record)
limits: small, fast pure-Python suites on one runner type; not a general claim

verify still exits 1 on natively passing suites whose failing tests are consistent with the denied network (pyjwt) or are matched by name without verify --record (marshmallow 2fc8207d, whose verdict also flips between a cold run and --rerun: the targeted run names files pytest's norecursedirs skips, the full run does not (RESULTS.md addendum; why the strategy differed was not recorded in runs 2-3); a limit until verify --record)
gates.next_action: the remaining fixed cost (interpreter and pytest start, base comparison) on small suites; consider steadier strategy inputs (a margin relative to the estimates, or the recorded choice reused for an unchanged suite) so close timings do not flip the strategy between runs
